classification_reason: The reviewed wheel implements its disclosed, explicitly started remote task-worker role. No hidden install-time payload, unauthorized persistence, credential-store theft, or concealed execution was established. Remote task execution, profiling and vendor identity alone cannot establish malicious intent. This classification does not imply safe execution of untrusted server-selected modules.
method: Static extraction and review of Python modules, entry points, package metadata and proxy manifest; individual cleave facts; source parse and wheel RECORD verification; cache-disabled full atomscan scan; independent download/hash comparison and static scan of the pinned macOS ARM64 proxy runtime. Neither the package nor its runtime was installed, imported or executed.

provenance.advisory_scope: The advisory identifies versions 6.26 and 6.28. Its observations are historical context, not proof about this 7.34 wheel. Several cited behaviors have materially changed: no apt/at/schtasks update script or embedded Aliyun key pair was found; WeChat-shaped notifications go through the authenticated vendor API; the proxy runtime and TLS/configuration paths are now constrained.

behavior: The console entry point is ryry.main:main. Service operation requires a configured authorization value and an explicit ryry service start. A successful authenticated task/config response is required during startup. No wheel install-time hook or .pth payload is present.

The service connects to wss://api.dalipen.com/aigc/task/connect, with HTTPS polling/result/configuration endpoints and an API fallback at aigc.zjtemplate.com. It accepts tasks, selects an enabled local widget, launches that widget with the current Python interpreter or dispatches to its daemon, and reports results.

While idle, periodic maintenance can query auto-deployment instructions and install or remove server-selected widget wheels/ZIPs. ZIPs are staged with traversal/symlink checks, optional requirements installation and an optional healthcheck.py probe before activation. Wheel URL installs use pip. These paths deliberately grant the server code-execution authority; task modules are not sandboxed.
CLI self-update checks PyPI and generates a detached Python pip/restart helper. This wheel does not contain the advisory's apt-get upgrade or at/schtasks restart sequence.

Host reporting includes hostname, public IP, CPU/memory/disk/GPU properties and a MAC/CPU-serial-derived device identifier. Task failures and a remote collect_log control action can upload the application's own service/update/proxy logs. No browser credential database or arbitrary home-directory secret sweep was found.

Cloud upload helpers use authenticated server-issued runtime Aliyun/R2 credentials. Legacy shared FTP credentials remain in source and can be used by FTP helper paths; this is a security/maintenance concern, not evidence that the wheel steals host credentials.

The private Mihomo process uses generated credentials and loopback listeners. Downloaded configuration is parsed with yaml.safe_load, filtered and normalized; remote listener/controller/path settings are not accepted. Explicit HTTP clients require TLS verification. Proxy environment values are scoped to owned child processes rather than changing OS proxy settings or globally monkey-patching unrelated clients.

The runtime download is pinned by archive and executable size/SHA-256. The downloaded darwin-arm64 executable exactly matches the official pinned upstream release. No additional executable is bundled inside the wheel.

Importing CLI modules can create local runtime/configuration directories and files. That is separate from running the remote service and is not an installation hook. No malicious agent-influence instruction document was found.

dependencies.coverage_limit: The wheel does not contain its PyPI dependency implementations. This triage did not install or independently scan those thirteen dependency distributions, the other five platform runtimes, authenticated server configuration, or future server-selected widget payloads. No claim that these were scanned is made.

corrections: Relocate task API/state/callback identifiers to source-name metadata, widget argv to process arguments, payload mapping access to mapping mechanics, and queue-handler calls to neutral dispatch. These observations do not establish remote control or a shell by themselves.

Relocate generic task/process/profile/archive-upload co-occurrences to neutral subprocess and HTTP subjects. Preserve original matchers and archive scopes, describe co-occurrence rather than asserting data flow, and consolidate the redundant widget-specific process composite into the broader process profile while retaining its argv atom. Update the profile-reporting consumer with the explicit argv requirement.

Relocate the broad ryry identity rules from malware/backdoor to dual-use/remote-admin. Package identity and ordinary host profiling do not distinguish a malicious variant. No package-name allowlist or blanket suppression was added.

Relocate the generic SOCKS listener/protocol composite from hostile C2 tunneling to notable proxy mechanics. Preserve its matchers and exclusions; place its FTP basename observation in filename metadata. The verified upstream Mihomo runtime now retains its SOCKS capability without a malicious-intent claim.

Fix the Python zero-version observation to require a module-level assignment in the Python AST. Local task/widget version defaults, class fields, comments, documentation strings and non-Python sources do not claim the package version is zero.

Restrict the urllib3 ProxyManager observation to qualified urllib3 call targets. A bare application class or arbitrary receiver with the same method name no longer claims urllib3 identity. Unresolved bare/import-alias calls are outside this tightened observation's coverage.

Require the fork-child guard to immediately test the same variable assigned from os.fork(), with zero equality or negation. Generic PID checks, different variables, different functions and intervening reassignment do not establish a fork-child branch.

Add a structured notable observation for a sys.executable/-m/pip argument vector, including unpacked dynamic arguments. It records invocation configuration without claiming execution or malicious installation.

Budget review: remove the unused payload/run_command co-occurrence in favor of its existing canonical call observation plus mapping read. Move the bare CommandId name and AppleScript NSTask class reference to source-name metadata, preserving their matchers/scopes and updating consumers. Dispatch and subprocess leaves remain within their 100-rule budgets.

validation.counting: Distinct emitted IDs at the wheel container; inherited member findings are not counted a second time. The separately fetched proxy runtime is reported separately.
validation.controls: Module/local/class/docstring version distinctions; linked fork branches, operator/variable/scope/reassignment near misses; qualified versus custom ProxyManager calls; pip argv structure; neutral remote worker and identity profiles; incomplete and renamed-member archives; criticality and retired-ID checks.
validation.make_validate: passed: hostile 668/668, benign 1478/1478, does-nothing 176/176, drop-exec 45/45, supply-chain 558/558, and all remaining configured suites
